Series::allclose¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

bool Series::allclose(const Series& other,
                      double rtol = 1e-5,
                      double atol = 1e-8,
                      bool equal_nan = false) const

What It Does¶

Returns one C++ bool: true when every broadcasted pair of values satisfies the isclose rule.

It is exactly self.isclose(other, rtol, atol, equal_nan).all().item<bool>() — the convenient reduction for a test assertion or a guard clause, where you want a single yes/no rather than a mask. When a comparison fails and you need to know which positions, drop down to isclose.

The per-position criterion, for receiver value a and reference value b:

close  iff  a == b                              (exact equality wins first)
       or   |a - b| <= atol + rtol * |b|        (and both a, b finite)

So exactly-equal finite values and matching infinities always pass; opposite infinities never do; and paired NaNs pass only with equal_nan = true. Every position must pass for allclose to return true — one failure anywhere is false.

Because rtol scales |b| — the other operand — allclose is not symmetric. a.allclose(b) and b.allclose(a) can disagree near the tolerance boundary.

Unlike equal, allclose requires the two operands to have the same dtype (it inherits isclose’s contract). It does, however, broadcast — so it can compare differently shaped operands, where equal would simply say false.

Parameters¶

other (const Series&): the reference values. Same dtype and platform as self; broadcast-compatible shape.

rtol (double, default 1e-5): nonnegative relative tolerance, multiplied by |other|.

atol (double, default 1e-8): nonnegative absolute floor. Dominates near zero.

equal_nan (bool, default false): when true, positions where both operands are NaN count as close.

Returns¶

bool true iff every broadcasted pair is close.

Raises¶

  • if the dtypes differ, or the platforms differ

  • if rtol < 0 or atol < 0

  • if the shapes are not broadcast-compatible

Gradient¶

Not applicable — allclose() returns a plain bool.

Examples¶

Example 1. A basic pass and a basic fail.

auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "within tol:  " << a.allclose(pluss::make_series({1.0 + 1e-9, 2.0, 3.0})) << "\n"
          << "one far off: " << a.allclose(pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.5, 3.0})) << "\n";

Output¶

within tol:  true
one far off: false

One position out of tolerance is enough to make the whole call false.

Example 2. Swapping the operands can flip the answer near the boundary, because rtol scales the reference.

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "a=9,  b=10: " << pluss::make_series({9.0}).allclose(pluss::make_series({10.0}), 0.1, 0.0) << "\n"
          << "a=10, b=9:  " << pluss::make_series({10.0}).allclose(pluss::make_series({9.0}), 0.1, 0.0) << "\n";

Output¶

a=9,  b=10: true
a=10, b=9:  false

Allowance 0.1 * 10 = 1 (error 1, passes) versus 0.1 * 9 = 0.9 (error 1, fails). If a symmetric notion of closeness matters, pick one operand as the canonical reference and always pass it in the same position.

Example 3. equal_nan repairs paired NaNs, but every other position must still pass on its own.

double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
double nan = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
auto a = pluss::make_series({inf, -inf, nan, 1.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({inf, inf, nan, 1.000001});
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "NaNs unequal: " << a.allclose(b) << "\n"
          << "NaNs equal:   " << a.allclose(b, 1e-5, 1e-8, true) << "\n";

Output¶

NaNs unequal: false
NaNs equal:   false

Even with equal_nan = true, -inf at position 1 does not match +inf, so the whole call is still false. equal_nan only fixes the NaN position, not the rest.

Example 4. An invalid tolerance is rejected by the shared isclose contract — note the diagnostic names isclose.

try {
  pluss::make_series({1.0}).allclose(pluss::make_series({1.0}), -1.0, 0.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

isclose: rtol must be greater than or equal to zero

Example 5. allclose requires matching dtype — where equal does not.

try {
  pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}).allclose(pluss::make_series({1, 2}));   // float vs int
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
std::cout << "equal() with the same pair: " << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0}).equal(pluss::make_series({1, 2})) << "\n";

Output¶

isclose: receiver and other must have the same dtype
equal() with the same pair: true

Convert first (other.to(self.dtype())) when the dtypes genuinely differ but you want a tolerant comparison.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Not symmetric — rtol scales |other|. Fix the reference operand’s position if closeness needs to be order-independent.

  • atol matters near zero. With atol = 0, values near zero almost never pass. Keep the nonzero default (or larger) for near-zero data.

  • Dtype must match — unlike equal. Convert with to first.

  • Broadcasting can compare differently shaped operands; if shape equality is part of the requirement, gate with is_same_size or use equal.

  • One failing position anywhere makes the whole call false — use isclose to find it.

Summary¶

allclose(other, rtol = 1e-5, atol = 1e-8, equal_nan = false) reduces isclose to a single bool:

  • true iff every broadcasted pair is close (exact-equal, or within atol + rtol*|b|)

  • asymmetric; atol carries the comparison near zero

  • broadcasts, but requires identical dtype (stricter than equal)

  • drop to isclose for the per-position mask
